assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reshaped how economists and policymakers understand technology, task content, trade exposure and wage inequality. The work combines clear identification (local labour-market trade shocks) with a coherent conceptual framework (the task approach, and the race between education and technology). Its influence extends beyond economics to political science, where it informs research on the political consequences of economic dislocation.
assessment.attribution: The task framework and skill-premium work are most associated with Autor and Katz. The China-shock identification is most associated with Autor and Hanson, with Dorn as a key coauthor. Other major contributors to the task literature (for example Levy and Murnane) are not credited here. Any three-name selection therefore omits someone, and the Katz-Murphy lineage adds further attribution complexity.
assessment.maturity: The core papers date from the 1990s to the early 2010s and have been tested by replication, extensions and debate. Subsequent work has refined rather than overturned the main findings. Timing is ripe.
uncertainties: Which subset of the four credited names best matches a coherent single citation.
Whether the China-shock results are judged robust enough in magnitude, given later critiques and heterogeneity across countries.
The task-based and trade-shock strands may be seen as two separate prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The heterogeneous-firm framework changed the field of international trade. It introduced firm-level selection, productivity-sorted exporting and a new channel for gains from trade, and it connected theory to micro data. It has generated a large literature and informed trade policy analysis.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central theoretical contribution, and Helpman, Melitz and Yeaple (2004) is another core paper. Helpman has a broader record in trade theory, including increasing returns and trade, and heterogeneous-firm work in the same period. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen, Kortum and others made closely related empirical and quantitative contributions and are not credited. Redding's quantitative and spatial extensions are real but more recent.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of confirmation and extension, with the framework embedded in standard graduate teaching and quantitative trade analysis.
uncertainties: Overlap with the Krugman 2008 prize on new trade theory may affect how the committee weighs the increment.
Credit allocation among the many empirical-heterogeneity contributors outside the credited names.
Whether adding Redding would better reflect the quantitative turn.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mian and Sufi's work provided micro-level evidence that household leverage and credit supply drove the housing boom, the bust and the depth of the Great Recession. It linked household balance sheets to aggregate demand and shifted macroeconomic thinking about the causes of credit cycles and the costs of financial crises. It combines new data, identification strategies and macroeconomic implications.
assessment.attribution: The papers and the book House of Debt are overwhelmingly a Mian-Sufi partnership. Campbell's household-finance work is valuable but a different contribution, so the two-person proposal fits best.
assessment.maturity: Core results date from about 2009 to 2015, and the empirical findings have been widely replicated, though interpretation continues to be debated. This is more recent than some competitors.
uncertainties: Whether the committee regards the field as sufficiently settled, given ongoing debate over the credit-supply versus expectations channel.
Overlap with the 2022 prize on banking and financial crises.
Whether the timing is premature compared with older, more established candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nominal rigidities, staggered pricing and the microfounded New Keynesian framework underlie modern monetary-policy analysis and practice. Policy rules, inflation targeting and the DSGE models used by central banks all draw on this body of work. Its practical and conceptual influence is very large.
assessment.attribution: Highly diffuse. Taylor (staggered contracts, policy rule), Calvo (time-dependent pricing), Woodford (the integrated theory of interest and prices), Gali (the empirical and theoretical NK model) and the Christiano-Eichenbaum-Evans medium-scale model are all central contributions. Any selection of at most three is contestable, and a cohesive citation is harder to write than for some other candidates.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with several decades of use. Some strands, notably the Taylor rule, are widely debated in policy terms.
uncertainties: Severe attribution difficulty with eight credited names and a three-laureate limit.
Earlier prizes (Lucas, Phelps, Kydland-Prescott, Bernanke) already cover adjacent areas.
Whether the committee views the post-2021 inflation episode as weakening or strengthening the framework.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Persson, Tabellini and Besley built modern political economics as a formal and empirical field. They analysed how constitutions, electoral rules and state capacity shape fiscal policy and economic outcomes, and they linked political institutions to economic development. This is a foundational contribution to understanding institutions, complementary to the 2024 prize but distinct in its focus on specific institutional design and its formal modelling.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are the closest pairing through the book Political Economics: Explaining Economic Policy and their constitutions work. Besley contributed in parallel, including with Persson on state capacity and with Case on political agency. Other contributors, such as Alesina, Acemoglu and Dixit, are outside the credited names. The three-name set is reasonable but not unambiguous.
assessment.maturity: The field began in the 1990s and has had decades of empirical testing. Some individual results are well supported, while others remain contested. Maturity is adequate.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2024 institutions prize, and the committee's appetite for a second institutions-themed award so soon.
Uneven empirical confirmation for specific constitutional-design predictions.
Breadth of the field makes a single sharp discovery citation harder.
I note this is also close to my own home discipline, and I have tried to apply the same criteria as for the other fields.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Kiyotaki and Moore's 1997 model of credit cycles showed how collateral constraints amplify and propagate shocks. This is a central mechanism in macro-finance and was used extensively to analyse the financial crisis. It provides a clear, tractable theory with lasting influence.
assessment.attribution: The credit-cycles model is clearly Kiyotaki-Moore. The related financial-accelerator work (Bernanke-Gertler) overlaps with the 2022 prize to Bernanke, while Gertler and Gilchrist's contributions are mainly later extensions and empirical work. A two-person proposal is the cleanest.
assessment.maturity: Nearly three decades of use and extension, with strong confirmation in the 2008 crisis aftermath.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 prize and with Bernanke-Gertler's earlier accelerator work.
Whether the committee prefers a broader macro-finance citation that includes Gertler.
Concentrated in theory with comparatively thinner direct empirical identification.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bayesian persuasion and information design opened a clear new theoretical area: how a sender optimally designs information to influence decision-makers. It has had broad applications in mechanism design, market regulation, platform design and political communication. It is conceptually crisp and has attracted a large literature.
assessment.attribution: Kamenica and Gentzkow (2011) is the foundational paper. Bergemann and Morris's information design and robust-predictions work is a related parallel stream. Selecting three requires choosing between these strands, and the exclusion of Bergemann is a clear cost.
assessment.maturity: Fifteen years old. The theory is established, but empirical or institutional confirmation is thinner than for older candidates.
uncertainties: Relative recency and limited empirical testing.
Attribution split between the persuasion and information-design strands.
Overlap with prior information-economics prizes (Akerlof-Spence-Stiglitz, mechanism design in 2007).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Piketty and Saez's top-income series, constructed from tax data across countries and long periods, transformed measurement of inequality and shaped academic and public debate. It created a new empirical standard and shifted attention to the top of the distribution. I value this partly as a measurement contribution, though I try to apply common criteria rather than favour my own methodological interests.
assessment.attribution: The 2003 top-incomes paper is Piketty-Saez, and the World Inequality Database effort is broader and collective. Zucman's offshore-wealth and distributional-accounts work is a later and partly separate contribution. Atkinson, who made major earlier contributions, is deceased and not credited. Capital in the Twenty-First Century is Piketty's alone and is more contested in its theoretical claims.
assessment.maturity: The data work has been extended widely and is broadly accepted, with ongoing methodological debate about wealth estimates and the capital-income-ratio argument.
uncertainties: Controversy over the theoretical claims (r > g) and over some wealth-distribution estimates.
Whether the committee views this as primarily measurement rather than a theoretical or causal discovery.
Whether Zucman should be included or the award reserved for a narrower citation.
